judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Content Standards (same grain, rank 1) in the Number strand: B5.1.2.2 requires understanding multiplication of a 2 or 3-digit number by a 2 or 3-digit number, while B5.1.2.4 requires understanding division of a 2 or 3-digit number by a 1 or 2-digit number. The high token/trigram overlap is mostly boilerplate ('demonstrate an understanding of ... digit number'), so it is not itself decisive; the substantive basis is operational: multi-digit division procedures depend on fluent multi-digit multiplication (estimating and subtracting partial products, multiplicative reasoning with 1- and 2-digit divisors), so proficiency with the multiplication standard supports success with the division standard. Same-rank direction is therefore grounded in the mathematical dependency of division on multiplication rather than on source code ordering. Evidence limitation: both endpoints have unresolved ancestry (no Strand/Sub-Strand hierarchy nodes supplied, only identity_scope Strand=Number in bounded source refs), no Learning Components were supplied, and source evidence is truncated (26 and 24 omitted items), so the judgment rests on the statement text and coordinates alone.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Content Standards in Strand 1 (NUMBER) at the same resolved rank (0). B4.1.2.6 (Number Operations sub-strand) asks learners to translate and solve word problems using the four basic operations on whole numbers, while B4.1.1.3 (Counting, Representation & Cardinality sub-strand) asks for understanding of factors, multiples and squared numbers. There is genuine conceptual coherence: factors, multiples and squares are multiplicative structures of whole numbers that reinforce and are reinforced by fluent multiplication/division work in problem solving. However, the supplied evidence shows no substantive same-rank developmental dependency in either direction — neither statement's bounded text indicates it presupposes the other, and neither is a deepening or extension of the other, so a permitted buildsTowards direction is not justified. Nomination signals (shared Grade/Strand ancestors, shared 'b4.1' code prefix, low token/trigram overlap limited to generic words such as 'and'/'numbers') are not themselves semantic evidence; the relatesTo judgment rests on the statement texts and sub-strand placement. Both endpoints have truncated source evidence (24 and 42 omitted items) and no Learning Components, which limits confidence in any stronger claim.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 (rank 2) Content Standards under Strand 1: Number, Sub-Strand 4: Ratios and Proportion, so the grain and scope match. B6.1.4.1 establishes understanding of the concept of ratios and their relationship to fractions and to multiplication/division of whole numbers; B6.1.4.2 explicitly requires understanding proportion 'and its relationship to ratios and rates' and applying proportional reasoning and rates to real-world problems. The second standard's own text makes ratio understanding the conceptual substrate it extends into proportion, rates, and applied reasoning, so proficiency in the ratio standard substantively supports success in the proportion standard. Same-rank direction is justified by this explicit textual dependency, not by code order or page proximity alone. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (26 omitted items each), which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (same rank, rank 0) under the same Content Standard B4.4.1.1 ('Demonstrate an understanding of many-to-one correspondence in displaying, and reading or interpreting, graphs') in Strand 4: Data. B4.4.1.1.2 asks learners to use an understanding of many-to-one correspondence to display or construct graphs, establishing the working command of the scale/correspondence device itself; B4.4.1.1.4 extends that command outward to authentic, unfamiliar graphs in print and electronic media, where learners must locate instances of many-to-one correspondence and describe the correspondence used. Constructing graphs with a chosen many-to-one correspondence substantively supports the later ability to recognise and articulate the correspondence embedded in others' media graphs, so the same-rank developmental direction runs second_to_first. The shared statement text and LC tokens ('many-to-one', 'correspondence', 'graphs') are corroborating, not sole, evidence; shared parent, code prefix, and rank proximity alone were not treated as sufficient. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text and LCs available.
